title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 34 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 34 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 34 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 34.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 34, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Josiah began to reign at eight years old
Josiah began to seek after the God of David in the eighth year
Josiah sent men to repair the house of the LORD in the eighteenth year
Josiah purged Judah and Jerusalem in the twelfth year
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah began to reign at eight years old
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:1 states that Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: How old was Josiah when he began to reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Eight years old
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:1 states Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: What did Josiah do that was right in the sight of the LORD?
options: Walked in the ways of David his father
Turned to the right hand and left
questions.correctAnswer: Walked in the ways of David his father
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:2 says Josiah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD and walked in the ways of David his father.

questions.question: In which year of Josiah's reign did he begin to seek after the God of David his father?
questions.correctAnswer: Eighth year
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:3 states that in the eighth year of his reign Josiah began to seek after the God of David his father.

questions.question: What did Josiah begin to purge in the twelfth year of his reign?
options: Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, groves, carved and molten images
The houses of the kings of Judah
The land of Manasseh and Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, groves, carved and molten images
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:3 states that in the twelfth year Josiah began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, groves, carved images, and molten images.

questions.question: What did Josiah do to the altars of Baalim?
options: Broke them down in his presence
questions.correctAnswer: Broke them down in his presence
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:4 states that they broke down the altars of Baalim in Josiah's presence.

questions.question: What did Josiah do with the carved and molten images after breaking them?
options: Broke them into pieces and made dust of them, strowing it upon graves
questions.correctAnswer: Broke them into pieces and made dust of them, strowing it upon graves
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:4 explains Josiah broke the carved and molten images into pieces, made dust of them, and strewed it upon the graves of those who sacrificed to them.

questions.question: What did Josiah do with the bones of the priests upon their altars?
options: Moved the bones to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt the bones
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:5 states Josiah burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars.

questions.question: Which regions did Josiah cleanse besides Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and Naphtali
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:6 states Josiah did likewise in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and Naphtali.

questions.question: Who did Josiah send to repair the house of the LORD in the eighteenth year of his reign?
options: Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder
The Levites who kept the doors
questions.correctAnswer: Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:8 states Josiah sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD.

questions.question: Who did Shaphan and the others deliver the money to when they came to repair the house of God?
options: The Levites who kept the doors
questions.correctAnswer: Hilkiah the high priest
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:9 states they delivered the money to Hilkiah the high priest.

questions.question: What was the money brought into the house of God used for?
options: Repairing and amending the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Repairing and amending the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:10 says the money was given to the workmen to repair and amend the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What materials were purchased with the money to repair the house of the LORD?
options: Hewn stone, timber for couplings, and flooring materials
Gold and silver for the temple treasures
Silk and fine linen for priests' garments
questions.correctAnswer: Hewn stone, timber for couplings, and flooring materials
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:11 states the money was given to artificers and builders to buy hewn stone, timber for couplings, and to floor the houses.

questions.question: Josiah declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left in his ways.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:2 states Josiah 'declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left.'

questions.question: Josiah burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars as part of cleansing Judah and Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:5 says Josiah burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 34 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 34 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were the overseers of the work in the house of the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 34:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Jahath and Obadiah
questions.explanation: The overseers of the work were Jahath and Obadiah, as stated in 2 Chronicles 34:12.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 34:13 promise will happen if someone serves faithfully in the house of the LORD?
options: They will be appointed as overseers
They will find a book of the law
They will receive the king's favor
questions.correctAnswer: They will be appointed as overseers
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:13 mentions that the Levites were overseers of the work, which implies that faithful service leads to appointment.

questions.question: What did Hilkiah the priest find in the house of the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 34:14?
questions.correctAnswer: The book of the law
questions.explanation: Hilkiah found a book of the law given by Moses in the house of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 34:14.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 34:21 indicate about the king's concern regarding the words of the book found?
questions.correctAnswer: He was deeply concerned
questions.explanation: The king expressed great concern about the wrath of the LORD due to the neglect of the law, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 34:21.

questions.question: What significant action did the king take upon hearing the words of the law in 2 Chronicles 34:19?
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes
questions.explanation: The king rent his clothes upon hearing the words of the law in 2 Chronicles 34:19, showing his distress.

questions.question: What was the role of the men who were over the bearers of burdens in 2 Chronicles 34:13?
questions.correctAnswer: To supervise the repairs
questions.explanation: These men were overseers of all that wrought the work in any manner of service, indicating their role in supervising repairs.

questions.question: What did Shaphan do after receiving the book from Hilkiah in 2 Chronicles 34:15?
options: He read it to the people
He delivered it to the king
questions.correctAnswer: He delivered it to the king
questions.explanation: Shaphan delivered the book to the king as stated in 2 Chronicles 34:15.

questions.question: How did the king react to the contents of the book read by Shaphan according to 2 Chronicles 34:18?
questions.correctAnswer: He was frightened
questions.explanation: The king was moved deeply, indicating a reaction of fear and concern upon hearing the law, as implied in 2 Chronicles 34:18.

questions.question: What did the king command after hearing the law in 2 Chronicles 34:20?
questions.correctAnswer: To seek the LORD
questions.explanation: The king commanded his officials to inquire of the LORD concerning the words of the book, indicating a desire to seek God, as stated in 2 Chronicles 34:20.

questions.question: Why did the king send men to Huldah the prophetess in 2 Chronicles 34:22?
options: To ask about the book found
questions.correctAnswer: To ask about the book found
questions.explanation: The king sent men to Huldah to inquire about the words of the book that was found, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 34:22.

questions.question: What was Josiah's approach to his faith as a king according to 2 Chronicles 34:2?
options: He followed the ways of his father
questions.correctAnswer: He followed the ways of his father
questions.explanation: Josiah did what was right in the sight of the LORD and walked in the ways of David his father, as noted in 2 Chronicles 34:2.

questions.question: What significant reform did Josiah initiate in the twelfth year of his reign according to 2 Chronicles 34:3?
options: He began to build the temple
He sought after the God of David
He made alliances with other nations
questions.correctAnswer: He sought after the God of David
questions.explanation: Josiah began to seek after the God of David his father in the twelfth year of his reign, as stated in 2 Chronicles 34:3.

questions.question: True or False: Hilkiah the priest delivered the book of the law to Shaphan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hilkiah delivered the book of the law to Shaphan according to 2 Chronicles 34:15.

questions.question: True or False: Josiah reigned in Jerusalem for 40 years.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Josiah reigned for 31 years, as stated in 2 Chronicles 34:1.

questions.question: True or False: The king did not care about the words of the law found by Hilkiah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The king was deeply concerned and rent his clothes upon hearing the words of the law, indicating he cared greatly, as noted in 2 Chronicles 34:19.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 34 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 34.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 34:24, what will the LORD bring upon the place and its inhabitants?
options: All the blessings written in the book
All the curses written in the book
questions.correctAnswer: All the curses written in the book
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:24 states that the LORD will bring evil upon this place and upon the inhabitants thereof, even all the curses that are written in the book.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 34:25, why does the LORD say His wrath will be poured out upon the place?
options: Because they have forsaken Him and burned incense to other gods
Because they built altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have forsaken Him and burned incense to other gods
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:25 explains that the wrath is due to forsaking the LORD and burning incense to other gods, provoking His anger.

questions.question: What reason does the LORD give in 2 Chronicles 34:27 for hearing the king's prayer?
options: Because the king had a mighty army
Because the king humbled himself and wept
Because the king built a temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because the king humbled himself and wept
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:27 states that the LORD heard the king because his heart was tender, he humbled himself, rent his clothes, and wept before God.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 34:28, what will happen to the king of Judah?
options: He will be gathered to his grave in peace and not see the evil to come
questions.correctAnswer: He will be gathered to his grave in peace and not see the evil to come
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:28 says the king will be gathered to his fathers and to his grave in peace, and his eyes will not see the evil coming on the place.

questions.question: What did King Josiah do after hearing the words of the book of the covenant, as described in 2 Chronicles 34:30?
options: He read all the words of the book aloud to the people
questions.correctAnswer: He read all the words of the book aloud to the people
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:30 states that the king went into the house of the LORD and read all the words of the book of the covenant to all the people.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 34:31, what covenant did King Josiah make before the LORD?
options: To build more altars for Baal
To walk after the LORD and keep His commandments with all his heart and soul
To ignore the law found in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: To walk after the LORD and keep His commandments with all his heart and soul
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:31 states Josiah made a covenant before the LORD to walk after Him and keep His commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and soul.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'נַעֲרָה' (na'arah) in 2 Chronicles 34:22 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetess
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 34:22, 'נַעֲרָה' (na'arah) refers to a young woman or maiden but is used here to denote the prophetess Huldah, indicating her role as a female prophet.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Chronicles 34:24-25 to emphasize the consequences of forsaking God?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:24-25 uses parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, repeating similar ideas about curses and wrath to emphasize consequences.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of covenant renewal and obedience found in 2 Chronicles 34:31?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 8:6-13
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:6-13 discusses the new covenant established through Christ, echoing the covenant renewal and obedience themes found in 2 Chronicles 34:31.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage parallels the discovery of the Book of the Law in 2 Chronicles 34:14-15?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 31:9-13
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:9-13 records Moses instructing the reading of the law to the people, paralleling the rediscovery and public reading of the Book of the Law in 2 Chronicles 34:14-15.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the king sending for the elders of Judah and Jerusalem in 2 Chronicles 34:29?
options: The LORD's message to the prophetess Huldah
The burning of the bones of the priests
The discovery of the Book of the Law
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD's message to the prophetess Huldah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:29 follows the delivery of the LORD's message to Huldah in verses 23-28, which precedes the gathering of the elders.

questions.question: How does the chapter 34 describe King Josiah's reforms in relation to idolatry in 2 Chronicles 34:33?
options: He tolerated some idols for political reasons
He took away all abominations and made the people serve the LORD
He built new altars to foreign gods
questions.correctAnswer: He took away all abominations and made the people serve the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:33 explains Josiah removed all abominations and ensured the people served the LORD their God throughout his reign.

questions.question: What is the significance of Josiah's tearing of his clothes upon hearing the words of the law in 2 Chronicles 34:19?
options: It signifies mourning, repentance, and humility before God
It was a royal fashion statement
It was a sign of defiance
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies mourning, repentance, and humility before God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:19 shows Josiah's tearing of clothes as a traditional Hebrew expression of mourning and repentance in response to the law's message.

questions.question: What typological foreshadowing can be seen in Josiah's covenant renewal in 2 Chronicles 34:31?
options: Foreshadowing of Christ's new covenant through obedience and heart commitment
Foreshadowing of the golden calf incident
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing of Christ's new covenant through obedience and heart commitment
questions.explanation: Josiah's sincere covenant renewal with all his heart (2 Chronicles 34:31) prefigures the New Testament new covenant of grace and obedience through Christ, as highlighted in Hebrews 8.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 34:32, the inhabitants of Jerusalem and Benjamin stood to the covenant and did not depart from following the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:32 states that the inhabitants of Jerusalem and Benjamin stood to the covenant and followed the LORD, confirming this statement.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 34 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 34 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 34:2 teach about human sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves steadfast obedience without wavering.
Sanctification is solely a moment of initial conversion.
Sanctification happens independently of divine influence.
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves steadfast obedience without wavering.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:2 states Josiah 'did that which was right in the sight of the LORD... and declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left,' implying sanctification is ongoing obedience and faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment and human responsibility is taught in 2 Chronicles 34:21?
options: God’s wrath is poured out because of the fathers’ failure to keep His word.
God’s wrath is arbitrary and unrelated to human actions.
God’s judgment only affects future generations, not the present.
God’s wrath is unconditional and cannot be averted by repentance.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath is poured out because of the fathers’ failure to keep His word.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:21 explains the king’s inquiry to God about the wrath poured out due to the ancestors’ disobedience, emphasizing responsibility for covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of the Word of God in covenant renewal is taught in 2 Chronicles 34:30?
options: The public reading of the covenantal law initiates communal covenant renewal.
Covenant renewal is independent of the knowledge of the law.
Only private meditation on the law is required for covenant renewal.
Rituals alone can renew the covenant without the law’s involvement.
questions.correctAnswer: The public reading of the covenantal law initiates communal covenant renewal.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:30 shows Josiah reading the words of the book of the covenant publicly, leading to a covenant renewal among all the people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 34:27 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Chronicles 34:27 shows God’s merciful response to Josiah’s humble repentance despite the coming judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 2 Chronicles 34:24 in relation to judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:24 emphasizes God’s righteous judgment against idolatry, revealing His holiness and intolerance of sin.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 34:14–15 connect to the broader biblical theme of the rediscovery of God's law and covenant renewal?
options: It prefigures the Deuteronomic reforms emphasizing covenant fidelity.
It introduces a new legal code unrelated to the Mosaic covenant.
It shows the abandonment of the law for prophetic revelation.
It marks the end of all covenantal requirements.
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the Deuteronomic reforms emphasizing covenant fidelity.
questions.explanation: The discovery of the book of the law in 2 Chronicles 34:14–15 anticipates the renewed covenant focus seen in Deuteronomy and later biblical reform movements.

questions.question: How does Josiah’s covenantal renewal in 2 Chronicles 34:31 anticipate the New Testament call to wholehearted discipleship?
options: It exemplifies total commitment to God’s commandments with heart and soul.
It focuses exclusively on external ritual observance without inner change.
It advocates for selective obedience to only the easy commandments.
It rejects the necessity of covenant faithfulness.
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies total commitment to God’s commandments with heart and soul.
questions.explanation: Verse 31 presents Josiah’s covenant commitment 'with all his heart, and with all his soul,' paralleling Jesus’ call to love God fully (Matthew 22:37).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 34:2 and 34:33 teach about covenant faithfulness and renewal?
options: True covenant renewal involves both personal obedience and nationwide reform.
Covenant renewal is purely symbolic and does not affect behavior.
Faithfulness is irrelevant to covenant life.
Renewal requires only the king’s compliance, not the people’s.
questions.correctAnswer: True covenant renewal involves both personal obedience and nationwide reform.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 34:2 shows Josiah’s personal obedience; 34:33 reveals national purging of abominations and commitment to serve God, indicating covenant renewal is holistic.

questions.question: What doctrine about the relationship between law discovery and divine revelation is taught by 2 Chronicles 34:14 and 34:18?
options: The rediscovery of the law initiates divine communication and prophetic response.
The law is irrelevant to divine revelation.
Divine revelation replaces the law entirely.
The law discovery discourages inquiry of God.
questions.correctAnswer: The rediscovery of the law initiates divine communication and prophetic response.
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes finding the law, verse 18 shows reading it to the king, prompting divine inquiry, illustrating law as a catalyst for revelation.

questions.question: What synthesis on God’s justice and mercy is taught by 2 Chronicles 34:24 and 34:27?
options: God executes judgment on sin but mercifully responds to genuine repentance.
God is merciful and ignores justice.
God’s justice is harsh and unrelenting without mercy.
God’s mercy negates the need for repentance.
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment on sin but mercifully responds to genuine repentance.
questions.explanation: Verses 24 and 27 show God pronouncing judgment but also hearing Josiah’s humble heart, demonstrating justice tempered with mercy.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Josiah’s reforms were purely political and not religious. What does 2 Chronicles 34:8–21 actually teach?
options: Josiah’s reforms were motivated by genuine religious conviction and concern for covenant faithfulness.
The reforms were only political maneuvers to consolidate power.
The reforms ignored the law and focused on political alliances.
Josiah rejected any religious motivation for his actions.
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah’s reforms were motivated by genuine religious conviction and concern for covenant faithfulness.
questions.explanation: Verses 8–21 describe discovering the law, concern over divine wrath, and seeking the Lord, showing sincere religious motivation.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s providential preservation of His word is taught in 2 Chronicles 34:14?
options: God preserves His law through generations despite human neglect.
God’s word is lost permanently once forgotten.
The law is unimportant to God’s covenant.
God replaces His law with new revelations regularly.
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves His law through generations despite human neglect.
questions.explanation: Verse 14 speaks of the book of the law found in the house of the LORD, showing divine preservation of the word.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's response to Josiah’s humility in 2 Chronicles 34:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Compassion
questions.explanation: God hears Josiah’s humble and repentant heart and promises peace at death, showing compassion (verse 27).

questions.question: What theological synthesis about covenant renewal and communal responsibility is taught by 2 Chronicles 34:30 and 34:32?
options: Covenant renewal requires corporate commitment, not just individual resolve.
Covenant renewal is an individual act with no communal implications.
Renewal is limited to the king alone.
Communal involvement is irrelevant in covenant fidelity.
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant renewal requires corporate commitment, not just individual resolve.
questions.explanation: Verse 30 shows the king reading the covenant; verse 32 shows the people standing to it, indicating communal responsibility.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 34:4–5 illustrate the theological principle of purging idolatry as necessary for covenant holiness?
options: Removing idols and their remnants is essential to restore covenant purity.
Idolatry can coexist with covenant faithfulness.
Idolatry is irrelevant to covenant holiness.
Only internal faith matters, not external purging.
questions.correctAnswer: Removing idols and their remnants is essential to restore covenant purity.
questions.explanation: Verses 4–5 describe breaking down altars and burning priests’ bones, symbolizing thorough cleansing for holiness.
